title: Mental Representations
coreMove: Turn practice into the construction and testing of a better inner model of the task.
sourcePressure: The chapter claims experts perform better because rich domain-specific mental representations change what they notice, remember, predict, and correct. Frozen sidecar for chapter 3 contains no traceable named figure, study, place, date, or artifact beyond the authors and chapter mechanism; sourceAnchors stays empty rather than inventing one.
chapterSpecificMisunderstanding: The weak version treats expert speed as more facts, magic intuition, or general intelligence.

exampleOpeningDiversity.rule: no more than 2 of the 6 examples may open with the pattern 'At HH:MM, <Name> <verb>s'
exampleOpeningDiversity.requiredOpenings: at least 4 distinct opening devices across the 6 examples, drawn from: timestamp+name+action, dialogue first line, sensory detail first, second-person 'You' direct address, retrospective 'It took her three weeks to see', question-as-hook, environmental detail before any human
exampleOpeningDiversity.rationale: C8 catches Cartesian repetition of phrases but not the deeper template of 'timestamp + named protagonist + prop + decision' that makes 6 examples feel like 1 example with name swaps

rhythmVariety.deepReadParagraphLengthMix: at least one paragraph 3 sentences or shorter, at least one paragraph 5+ sentences, at least one one-sentence punch line
rhythmVariety.fullReadInterludeRequirement: at least one paragraph that breaks the scene-then-rule rhythm: a question to the reader, a research aside, a direct second-person passage, or a brief historical reference
rhythmVariety.forbiddenRhythm: every paragraph following the pattern 'concrete anchor sentence -> abstract rule sentence -> elaboration sentence'

exampleSpecs.domain: aircraft maintenance troubleshooting a recurring cabin pressure alert
exampleSpecs.audience: a technician learning to organize signals instead of chasing parts
exampleSpecs.stakes: one wrong replacement keeps an aircraft grounded through another rotation
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Rachel draws the alert sequence on a maintenance cart, predicts the valve check before opening the panel, and updates the diagram when the gauge proves her model incomplete
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a pressure gauge clipped to a silver maintenance cart

exampleSpecs.domain: sourdough bakery crumb diagnosis after overnight fermentation
exampleSpecs.audience: a baker whose recipes work until temperature changes
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wholesale order could fail because he sees loaves as recipes rather than cues
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Andrew sketches what a good crumb should show, slices two test loaves, and changes his fermentation model when the tunnels reveal overproofing
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a serrated knife opening a loaf with tunnels under the crust

exampleSpecs.domain: fire-dispatch map reading during a multi-unit response drill
exampleSpecs.audience: a dispatcher who knows street names but not movement patterns
exampleSpecs.stakes: units lose minutes when she cannot predict which route will jam next
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Lea pauses before assigning a unit, marks likely traffic choke points on acetate, and checks the prediction against radio reports before the next assignment
exampleSpecs.firstImage: clear acetate sliding over a city response map
mustAvoid: ambulance bay replay from old draft

exampleSpecs.domain: wildlife photographer reading bird movement before a shot
exampleSpecs.audience: a self-taught photographer who keeps reacting after the bird leaves
exampleSpecs.stakes: a rare migration window closes before he learns to anticipate behavior
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Niklas reviews six missed frames, groups wing tilt with perch choice, predicts the next takeoff, and records whether the pattern holds
exampleSpecs.firstImage: six blurred frames pinned above a muddy boot tray

exampleSpecs.domain: litigation associate structuring a deposition outline
exampleSpecs.audience: a young lawyer who has facts but no case map
exampleSpecs.stakes: a witness can bury the key admission if questions stay in chronological order
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: You see Chiara move facts from a timeline into a causation map, predict the evasive answer, and rewrite the next question around the missing link
exampleSpecs.firstImage: colored tabs migrating from a timeline to a blank causation chart

exampleSpecs.domain: orchestra librarian spotting score-part mismatches before rehearsal
exampleSpecs.audience: a behind-the-scenes music worker who wants faster error detection
exampleSpecs.stakes: a wrong part wastes rehearsal minutes across seventy players
exampleSpecs.requiredBeat: Akira compares the conductor score with one marked part, predicts where transposition errors cluster, and builds a checklist from the mismatch pattern
exampleSpecs.firstImage: a bassoon part opened beside a conductor score with colored flags

skillTargets: define mental representations as working models
choose practice that improves prediction and cue selection
distinguish organized structure from memorized fragments
analyze when an expert model needs correction

tryThisNowSpec: Before your next practice rep, write what good should look like in three cues. After the rep, mark which cue failed and revise the model in one sentence.
